Ticket Id: 24528

03/05/2014

Dr Malcolm Still
Rheumatologist
5 Grant ST
Fairmont

Dear Dr Still,
RE: Mr James Seymour
DOB: 19/03/1953

I am writing to refer this patient who is demonstrating signs and symptoms presumptive of gout for further
investigations and management.

The patient has been having constant attacks of inflammation since 2010 for which he has been taking
colchicine, indomethacin and allopurinol. Although he has been a non-smoker since 1994, his alcohol
consumption is excessive.

Initially, when the patient presented it to me on 25/04/2014, he was complaining of his third attack of gout
in the last eight months. On examination, his first left toe was red in colour, moderately inflamed, and very
painful. However, his other joints were normal. Therefore, paracetamol and oxycodone were commenced
in addition to the ongoing management of colchicine and indomethacin. Furthermore, I reinforced the
importance of healthy diet compliance and to decrease the amount of alcohol intake.

Today, the patient's X-ray confirmed mildly degenerative changes of the left first metatarsophalangeal
joint. Moreover, his MCH (32.3 pg), urate (0.48) and CRP (6.0 mg/L) readings were slightly increased.
Accordingly, allopurinol was instituted along with the adjustment of oxycodone intake.

Based on the patient's father history of rheumatoid arthritis, he insisted to be referred. It would be grateful   Commented [JG1]: I
if you could discuss with him the synovial fluid pathology results which are enclosed to my letter.               Commented [JG2]: with


Thank you for your expert care and kindly feel free to contact me if any more information is required.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
